title: Area, Surface Area and Volume
seo_title: Grade 7 Area, Surface Area and Volume Worksheets: Triangles, Trapezoids and Prisms
standard_text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 area, surface area and volume worksheets: triangles, trapezoids and composite shapes, volume and surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms, and real-world problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.

body_html:
Area, surface area and volume

Area covers a flat shape. Surface area covers all the faces of a solid. Volume fills the space inside. Split a hard shape into rectangles and triangles, then add or subtract.

ShapeFormulaUnits
TriangleA = ½ × b × hsquare units
TrapezoidA = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × hsquare units
Prism volumeV = (area of base) × heightcubic units
Box volumeV = l × w × hcubic units
Box surface areaSA = 2lw + 2lh + 2whsquare units
Example

A tent is a triangular prism: triangle base 6 ft, height 4 ft, length 8 ft. How much space is inside?

Base area = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 ft².

Volume = 12 × 8 = 96 ft³.

Answer: 96 ft³

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the ½ for a triangle.
  • Using the slanted side instead of the height.
  • Mixing up surface area (square units) and volume (cubic units).
  • Counting only 3 faces of a box: there are 6.

faq.q: What is the difference between surface area and volume?
faq.a: Surface area is the total area of the outside faces, in square units. Volume is the space inside, in cubic units.

faq.q: How do you find the volume of a triangular prism?
faq.a: Find the area of the triangle (½ × base × height), then multiply by the length of the prism.

faq.q: How do you find the surface area of a box?
faq.a: Add the areas of all 6 faces: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. A 5 × 3 × 4 box has SA = 2(15 + 20 + 12) = 94.

faq.q: How do I find the area of a composite shape?
faq.a: Split it into rectangles and triangles, find each area, then add them. Subtract any parts that are cut out.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². Not 60: that forgets the ½. Use the height, not the slanted side.

items.e: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm². Not 40: that forgets the ½. Use the height, not the slanted side.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 14 × 6 = 42 cm². Not 84: that forgets the ½. Use the height, not the slanted side.

Find the volume of the rectangular prism (5 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm).
items.e: V = l × w × h = 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cm³. Not 94: that is the surface area.

items.q: Find the volume of the rectangular prism (8 cm by 2 cm by 6 cm).
items.e: V = l × w × h = 8 × 2 × 6 = 96 cm³. Not 152: that is the surface area.

items.q: Find the volume of the rectangular prism (10 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm).
items.e: V = l × w × h = 10 × 4 × 3 = 120 cm³. Not 164: that is the surface area.

items.q: Find the volume of the rectangular prism (7 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm).
items.e: V = l × w × h = 7 × 5 × 2 = 70 cm³. Not 118: that is the surface area.

items.q: Find the volume of the rectangular prism (6 cm by 6 cm by 6 cm).
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 cm³. Not 216: that is the surface area.

items.q: Find the volume of the rectangular prism (12 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm).
items.e: V = l × w × h = 12 × 3 × 5 = 180 cm³. Not 222: that is the surface area.

items.q: A triangular prism has a triangle base with base 6 in. and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in. long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the triangle = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 in². V = 12 × 10 = 120 in³. Not 240: that forgets the ½.

items.q: A triangular prism has a triangle base with base 8 in. and height 3 in. The prism is 5 in. long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the triangle = ½ × 8 × 3 = 12 in². V = 12 × 5 = 60 in³. Not 120: that forgets the ½.

items.q: A triangular prism has a triangle base with base 5 in. and height 6 in. The prism is 7 in. long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the triangle = ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 in². V = 15 × 7 = 105 in³. Not 210: that forgets the ½.

items.q: A triangular prism has a triangle base with base 10 in. and height 4 in. The prism is 9 in. long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the triangle = ½ × 10 × 4 = 20 in². V = 20 × 9 = 180 in³. Not 360: that forgets the ½.

items.q: A triangular prism has a triangle base with base 12 in. and height 5 in. The prism is 4 in. long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the triangle = ½ × 12 × 5 = 30 in². V = 30 × 4 = 120 in³. Not 240: that forgets the ½.

Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 5 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(5 × 3) + 2(5 × 4) + 2(3 × 4) = 30 + 40 + 24 = 94 cm². Not 47: count all 6 faces.

items.q: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 6 cm by 2 cm by 3 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(6 × 2) + 2(6 × 3) + 2(2 × 3) = 24 + 36 + 12 = 72 cm². Not 36: count all 6 faces.

items.q: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 8 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(8 × 5) + 2(8 × 2) + 2(5 × 2) = 80 + 32 + 20 = 132 cm². Not 66: count all 6 faces.

items.q: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 4 cm by 4 cm by 4 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(4 × 4) + 2(4 × 4) + 2(4 × 4) = 32 + 32 + 32 = 96 cm². Not 48: count all 6 faces.

items.q: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 10 cm by 6 cm by 3 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(10 × 6) + 2(10 × 3) + 2(6 × 3) = 120 + 60 + 36 = 216 cm². Not 108: count all 6 faces.

items.q: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 7 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(7 × 3) + 2(7 × 5) + 2(3 × 5) = 42 + 70 + 30 = 142 cm². Not 71: count all 6 faces.

items.q: Find the surface area of a rectangular prism 9 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm.
items.e: Three pairs of faces: 2(9 × 2) + 2(9 × 4) + 2(2 × 4) = 36 + 72 + 16 = 124 cm². Not 62: count all 6 faces.

A triangular prism has right-triangle bases with legs 6 cm and 8 cm and hypotenuse 10 cm. The prism is 5 cm long. What is its surface area?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48. Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 5 = 120. Total 168 cm².

items.q: A triangular prism has right-triangle bases with legs 3 cm and 4 cm and hypotenuse 5 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its surface area?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 3 × 4 = 12. Three rectangles: (3 + 4 + 5) × 10 = 120. Total 132 cm².

items.q: A triangular prism has right-triangle bases with legs 5 cm and 12 cm and hypotenuse 13 cm. The prism is 4 cm long. What is its surface area?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 5 × 12 = 60. Three rectangles: (5 + 12 + 13) × 4 = 120. Total 180 cm².

items.q: A triangular prism has right-triangle bases with legs 9 cm and 12 cm and hypotenuse 15 cm. The prism is 6 cm long. What is its surface area?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 9 × 12 = 108. Three rectangles: (9 + 12 + 15) × 6 = 216. Total 324 cm².

items.q: Which measures the space inside a box?
items.e: Volume (cubic units) measures the space inside. Surface area (square units) measures the outside covering.

items.q: Wrapping paper covers a gift box. Which do you need to find?
items.e: Paper covers the outside faces, so you need the surface area.

items.q: Which unit fits a surface area?
items.e: Surface area is an area, so it uses square units.

items.q: A net of a rectangular prism has how many rectangles?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, so its net has 6 rectangles.

items.q: Doubling every edge of a cube makes its volume how many times as large?
items.e: Volume = s³. (2s)³ = 8s³. (Surface area becomes 4 times as large.)
